OTHER RATES AND CHARGES
Distributed Generation - Produced Energy – Residential Customers with Bi-directional meters installed on or before April 15, 2025 for Rate Codes E01 to E08
Energy produced by residential customers with distributed generation resources will be credited to the customer by
the District of Summerland as follows:
i. In each billing cycle, produced energy will be credited at the corresponding energy charge of the rate code
for the customer type (residential) until the customer reaches net-zero (i.e., to a maximum of the customer’s
consumption in that billing cycle);
ii. Produced energy in excess of consumption will carry forward to the next billing cycle as ‘banked’ kWh’s.
Any ‘banked’ kWh’s remaining at the end of the calendar year will be credited to the customer at the
prevailing avoided cost of energy purchase. iii. Any surplus over $100, as of December 31, will be paid to the customer.
iv. Any surplus of $100 or less, as of December 31, will be applied as a credit to the customer’s electric
account. Distributed Generation - Produced Energy - Customers with Bi-directional meters installed after April 15, 2025
Energy produced will be credited to the customer by the District of Summerland as follows: i. In each billing cycle, surplus produced energy will be credited at the wholesale rate (rate schedule 40 in the
FortisBC electric tariff) and applied to the Customer’s monthly utility invoice. ii. Any surplus over $300 as of December 31 will be paid to the customer.
iii. Any surplus of $300 or less as of December 31 will be applied as a credit to the customer’s electric account.
Electrical Vehicle Charging Stations
These rates apply for usage at District owned electric vehicle charging stations. i. Level 2 (7.2 W) Stations $ 2.00 per hour
ii. Level 3 (50 W) Stations $18.00 per hour
